body: I'm using vim script plugin which is for R language [NVIM-R](https://github.com/jalvesaq/Nvim-R) and it has around 50 or so mappings that all start with localleader `\`. `Mini.clue` gets the mappings but doesn't get the descriptions (probably because it's vim script that has no `desc`) like below I checked the source code of the mapping in `NVIM-R` plugin and it was like so: ```vim function RCreateCommentMaps() RCreateMapsWrapper("ni", "RToggleComment", "xx", ':call RComment("normal")') RCreateMapsWrapper("v", "RToggleComment", "xx", ':call RComment("selection")') RCreateMapsWrapper("ni", "RSimpleComment", "xc", ':call RSimpleCommentLine("normal", "c")') RCreateMapsWrapper("v", "RSimpleComment", "xc", ':call RSimpleCommentLine("selection", "c")') RCreateMapsWrapper("ni", "RSimpleUnComment", "xu", ':call RSimpleCommentLine("normal", "u")') RCreateMapsWrapper("v", "RSimpleUnComment", "xu", ':call RSimpleCommentLine("selection", "u")') RCreateMapsWrapper("ni", "RRightComment", ";", ':call MovePosRCodeComment("normal")') RCreateMapsWrapper("v", "RRightComment", ";", ':call MovePosRCodeComment("selection")') end ``` so the keymapping function is like that: ```vim function RCreateMaps(type, plug, combo, target) ``` Because I don't want to write desc for 50 mappings, I'm okay with getting the `plug` part as `desc` so I wrote a wrapper function to get it but didn't work unfortunately. is there a way to do that with `mini.clue`, if not, I'll write description for the the keymapping but I'm not sure how to do that without affecting my config. I wan thinking of [mapx.nvim](https://github.com/b0o/mapx.nvim) plugin. ```lua require('mapx').nnoremap('r', ':RunRCommand', {desc = 'Run R command'}) ``` any help would be really appreciated

I'm using vim script plugin which is for R language NVIM-R and it has around 50 or so mappings that all start with localleader \.

Mini.clue gets the mappings but doesn't get the descriptions (probably because it's vim script that has no desc) like below

I checked the source code of the mapping in NVIM-R plugin and it was like so:

   function RCreateCommentMaps()
        RCreateMapsWrapper("ni", "RToggleComment", "xx", ':call RComment("normal")')
        RCreateMapsWrapper("v", "RToggleComment", "xx", ':call RComment("selection")')
        RCreateMapsWrapper("ni", "RSimpleComment", "xc", ':call RSimpleCommentLine("normal", "c")')
        RCreateMapsWrapper("v", "RSimpleComment", "xc", ':call RSimpleCommentLine("selection", "c")')
        RCreateMapsWrapper("ni", "RSimpleUnComment", "xu", ':call RSimpleCommentLine("normal", "u")')
        RCreateMapsWrapper("v", "RSimpleUnComment", "xu", ':call RSimpleCommentLine("selection", "u")')
        RCreateMapsWrapper("ni", "RRightComment", ";", ':call MovePosRCodeComment("normal")')
        RCreateMapsWrapper("v", "RRightComment", ";", ':call MovePosRCodeComment("selection")')
      end

so the keymapping function is like that:

function RCreateMaps(type, plug, combo, target)

Because I don't want to write desc for 50 mappings, I'm okay with getting the plug part as desc so I wrote a wrapper function to get it but didn't work unfortunately.

is there a way to do that with mini.clue, if not, I'll write description for the the keymapping but I'm not sure how to do that without affecting my config. I wan thinking of mapx.nvim plugin.

require('mapx').nnoremap('<localleader>r', ':RunRCommand<CR>', {desc = 'Run R command'})

any help would be really appreciated

comment_data.body: 'mini.clue' indeed uses mapping description to infer what information to shoe. The intentional decision is to [make mapping description take priority over manually defined clues in `config.clues`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/1fdbb864e2015eb6f501394d593630f825154385/doc/mini-clue.txt#L79-L82). The suggested solution is to use [`set_mapping_desc()`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/1fdbb864e2015eb6f501394d593630f825154385/doc/mini-clue.txt#L622) to update mapping description.

reply_data.body:
That is a lot of dedicated effort from you, my fellow R user :)

I am not sure what might be wrong with your solutions. My first guess would be that they get executed *before* filetype mappings from 'Nvim-R' are created. Although that would result in an error from `set_mapping_desc()`... Not sure at all.

Here is the solution I got working and general approach I'd recommend:
- This is the content of Neovim Lua config (either directly in '~/.config/nvim/init.lua' or in its sourced module):
```lua
-- Set custom descriptions to mappings coming from 'nvim-R'
local has_miniclue, miniclue = pcall(require, 'mini.clue')
if not has_miniclue then return end

miniclue.set_mapping_desc('n', '<localleader>fa', 'Send "echo" "down"')
miniclue.set_mapping_desc('v', '<localleader>fa', 'Send "echo" "down"')
```

- Create '~/.config/nvim/after/ftplugin/r.lua' file with the following content:
```lua
-- Set custom descriptions to mappings coming from 'nvim-R'
local has_miniclue, miniclue = pcall(require, 'mini.clue')
if not has_miniclue then return end

miniclue.set_mapping_desc('n', '<localleader>fa', 'Send "echo" "down"')
miniclue.set_mapping_desc('v', '<localleader>fa', 'Send "echo" "down"')
```

The first step sets up proper 'mini.clue' triggers. The second step is what gets executed when buffer is being set an `r` filetype. Having it in 'after' directory means that this code will be executed *after* all other plugin-specific code. This is the usual approach for user to customize filetype-specific behavior.

Note, that with '~/.config/nvim' this assumes Unix style setup; if you are on Windows, use '~/AppData/Local/nvim'.

------

However, the proper solution here I see is to make an issue/PR to 'Nvim-R' which creates mappings with descriptions. This would require using condition on Neovim>=0.7 (when mapping descriptions were introduced). That repo seems active, so this might result in a success.
